selected.text: Thy letter hath come before the Throne, adorned with the mention of thy Lord and sanctified from all else. By My life! It is better for thee than all that thou hast done before, for there hath been ordained for him whose letter reacheth the Throne after its arrival in the Most Great Prison the reward of one who hath attained His presence, beheld His countenance, and heard what His tongue hath uttered. This is indeed a great bounty.
selected.reason: Correspondence enables connection despite imprisonment.

selected.text: That which thou didst send hath been presented and was accepted. Give thanks unto thy Lord for this mighty favor. The cord was not accepted before, but that which thou didst send was accepted before the All-Merciful. Well is it with thee!
selected.reason: Different responses to offered gifts prevent assumptions of automatic acceptance.

selected.text: Divine favors have been and are directed towards you. God willing, the friends in that land who have drunk from the Kawthar of eternity and who gaze toward the Most Exalted Horizon will not neglect your affairs and will exert their utmost efforts to improve them according to their capacity.
selected.reason: Friends should improve a recipient's circumstances according to capacity.

selected.text: He who hath loved Me and drunk the choice wine of attainment from the hand of My bounty hath desired to return to the twigs of the Tree and the loved ones of the blessed Word, bearing new gifts and wondrous presents of divine utterances and heavenly words.
selected.reason: Divine writings themselves become gifts carried to others.

selected.text: Thou hast spent what thou hadst in the path of God - to this the Lord of all being bears witness. God will soon reward thee for what thou hast done in His love.
selected.reason: Recognizes costly personal sacrifice in giving.

selected.text: A single word from thee was presented at the Most Holy Court, before the face of the Wronged One, and that word found acceptance.
selected.reason: Even a single offered word can receive acknowledgment.

selected.text: As regards Jinab-i-Mulla Muhammad-'Ali (Tafti), upon him be the Glory of God [Baha'u'llah], after presentation They stated that upon his arrival in prison he sent whatever he had, and permission was given to accept it, but until now We have not used it. And now, considering that he has again intended to send an amount, We will accept this sum provided that he also accepts this second amount from Us. This is a bounty
selected.reason: Acceptance of a second gift conditioned on receiving a gift in return.

selected.text: Glory be to Thee, O my God! These are honored servants and devoted handmaidens who have hastened to the fountain of Thy mercy and rushed to the shelter of Thy protection. They have forsaken their rest and bid farewell to their wealth, turning to the Kingdom of Beauty and supplicating to the Realm
selected.reason: Prayer recognizes sacrifice of rest and wealth.

selected.text: The editor of Al-Qahirah newspaper, Bashir Effendi Yusuf, wrote and sent a laudatory poem two months ago. Give him five liras with this letter.
selected.reason: Acknowledgment includes material recompense for a creative contribution.

selected.text: As for the sum that has been designated for 'Abdu'l-Baha's travel expenses, it is clear this action stems from utmost love and is evidence of steadfastness and firmness. I became infinitely grateful to you all and was pleased, and I beseech blessings for you from the Court of Unity, for giving leads to blessing. However, the means for travel have been prepared and all necessary expenses are ready - there is absolutely no lack or deficiency. Therefore, with utmost joy and pleasure the sum you have sent is being returned so that you may spend it on charitable causes.
selected.reason: Surplus travel contribution returned for charitable use.

selected.text: The silver picture frame, which was of exquisite Chinese craftsmanship and meant for holding the likeness of the Most Luminous Beauty, arrived through Haji Siyyid Javad
selected.reason: Craftsmanship crosses cultural boundaries in a devotional gift.

selected.text: His will was reviewed - it was written with the utmost joy and fragrance. A will should be like this - everyone should take it as an example.
selected.reason: A joyful will offers a distinct form of giving.

selected.text: The renewal of the spiritual gathering through the efforts of Muhammad Baqir Khan and Mirza Muhammad Ali Khan was most timely - blessed are they and excellent is their final abode.
selected.reason: Renewing a gathering is a collective contribution.

selected.text: The luminous page and portrait of the divine countenances of the spiritual friends was observed. From the luminosity of those spiritual faces, spirituality was attained and joy and delight shone forth in hearts. Although these were physical portraits, in truth a spiritual beauty was evident, for on their foreheads the manifest light of love was apparent.
selected.reason: Photographs mediate affection and spiritual remembrance.

selected.text: Whatever is sent from Rangoon for your necessary expenses is all accepted at the Divine Threshold. I hope that the contributor becomes a manifestation of bounty and blessing.
selected.reason: Contributions meet necessary personal expenses.

selected.text: The funds you sent for building the bath were accepted, but as it happened some friends were preparing to return but had treasure in their sleeve while their purse was empty. It was observed that the sweetness of spending it on the friends' journey exceeded the comfort and cleanliness of the bath. Therefore it was spent on their behalf for what was necessary, and so you should offer thanks at the Divine Threshold that you were enabled to render this service.
selected.reason: Funds redirected from a bath to urgent travel needs of friends.

selected.text: This thousand tumans has been telegraphed to Haji Amin to be sent immediately, and this sum of one thousand tumans will be sent by whatever means possible - be assured of this. … As for the expenses of the Holy House, write every year and they will be sent from here
selected.reason: Annual reporting sustains provision for a sacred house.

selected.text: The sum that you sent for the wronged handmaiden of God, the respected young lady Khanim Zia, was the cause of gratitude and satisfaction
selected.reason: Aid to a wronged woman makes relief personal and concrete.

selected.text: Your detailed letters were received and their contents brought joy to this grieving heart, for they detailed the sale of your house which you donated for the expenses of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar.
selected.reason: House sale offered for temple construction requires its own context.

selected.text: The sums that the illustrious Afnans and others have contributed and you have spent towards the expenditure of the Shrine of the Bab and the pilgrim house is most acceptable.
selected.reason: Funds support both shrine and pilgrim accommodation.

selected.text: The contribution ledger from various regions for the oppressed ones of Nayriz was received and read with utmost joy, and the receipts are being sent.
selected.reason: Relief ledger and receipts unite generosity with accountability.

selected.text: Since thy manner, deed, spirit and efforts have brought me such deep delight, I have sent the candelabrum you donated to the Sacred Shrine so that a sign from you may be preserved at that Blessed Threshold. This benevolence is for the kindness and generosity you have shown this youth.
selected.reason: Gift of a lamp linked with kindness toward a young person.

selected.text: Let His Holiness Sadru's-Sudur carry out whatever his heart desires. The purpose is that through Jenab-i-Amin who is there, they should experience no hardship
selected.reason: Arrangements should prevent hardship to the recipient.

selected.text: whatever they submitted to Jinab-i-Amin has all been received … You should reassure all the friends that whatever they submitted has all been received
selected.reason: Reassures all contributors that their gifts arrived.

selected.text: Praise be to God that Fadl'Ali Khan, after the ascension of the divine Nightingale (Andalib), arose in faithfulness and assists and takes care of the family of that noble soul.
selected.reason: Sustained care for a family after bereavement.

selected.text: Write to the Hakim-Bashi that I am very embarrassed by his troubles and am absolutely not willing for him to send any more funds.
selected.reason: Explicit refusal of further funds to protect a donor from trouble.

selected.text: Rustam Surush and other brothers and relatives had offered a piece of land near the sacred dust of the martyrs in God's path
selected.reason: Family cooperation in giving land near martyrs' resting place.

selected.text: The services thou didst render and the troubles thou didst endure during our stay in London were indeed considerable and worthy of praise. Nor shall I ever forget them
selected.reason: Travel hospitality and unseen practical work remembered.

selected.text: Write down the names of the friends who are partners and participants in this blessed purpose and who have rendered assistance, so that they may be recorded in this land and their blessed names may endure forever in the eternal world
selected.reason: Records the names of all partners in a shared purpose.

selected.text: of truth! Your letter was received. I have accepted the invitation of the Unity Church
selected.reason: Acceptance of an invitation extends fellowship beyond one community.

selected.text: The letter which thou didst send through Jinab-i-Mahmud-i-Mahmud had a most acceptable form of address, namely the words "Ya 'Abdu'l-Baha".
selected.reason: Preferred form of address expresses servitude rather than status.

selected.text: The services you rendered during the ascension of His Holiness the Afnan of the Blessed Tree, Aqa Mirza Aqa, were accepted and beloved at the Sacred Threshold of the Abha Beauty.
selected.reason: Acknowledges service during bereavement.

selected.text: and remain in the utmost joy, delight and radiance. A small expense and medicine was sent for Jinab-i-Tamaddun
selected.reason: Small financial help and medicine meet personal need.

selected.text: Regarding the memorial gathering for one who attained the meeting of his Lord, Aqa Muhammad Mustafa, you had written that through the effort of the Service Assembly and Jinab-i-Aqa Muhammad 'Ali Kashani it was arranged in the home of Jinab-i-Mu'avin Naraqi - this brought much joy.
selected.reason: A community memorial gathering is a gift of remembrance.

selected.text: I was extremely pleased that the matter of the Siyyids' Khums was resolved amicably.
selected.reason: Financial/religious dispute resolved amicably.

selected.text: I have the utmost love for you, and sending the photograph of the deceased Qa'im-Maqam brought the greatest joy. That portrait hangs in my bedroom and every morning when I wake up my eyes fall upon it.
selected.reason: Portrait of a deceased person sustains daily remembrance.

selected.text: the friends in Shiraz are thinking of helping the survivors of Yazd, to provide those famine-stricken ones with necessary sustenance
selected.reason: Community aid provides sustenance to famine-stricken survivors.

selected.text: You had truly shown kindness to the children and daughters of the Kingdom by interceding on behalf of Mirza Ali Akbar
selected.reason: Intercession for another person is a form of service.

selected.text: At Karpout the Acting Governor-General came to call on us--and with him brought ten car-loads of rice, ten sacks of barley, ten sheep, several baskets of rice, several bags of sugar, many pounds of butter, etc. These were sent as gifts by the Governor-General, Ezzat Pasha, to the Blessed Perfection
selected.reason: Reported hospitality and gifts during travel need their historical setting.

selected.text: That they have written that they gave four tumans to Jinab-i-Aqa Shaykh Hasan, upon him be Baha'u'llah's glory, and likewise nineteen qirans to the emigrants of the land of Sad, upon them be Baha'u'llah's glory, and similar instances - after being presented before the Most Holy and Most Exalted Presence, He said: "Whatever is given to the friends of God is acceptable and approved
selected.reason: Recognizes material assistance given directly to friends.

selected.text: regarding the remainder, according to the command they should act with moderation. The Blessed Tablet that was revealed concerning this matter and sent previously hath, God willing, arrived and they will peruse it
selected.reason: Moderation governs use of remaining resources.

selected.text: Regarding what was written about the funds, some time ago this servant, as commanded, wrote to Jinab-i-Haji Mirza Abu'l-Hasan (upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God) and emphasized that if they had any of the Huququ'llah with them and if sending it would be accomplished with joy and fragrance, they should send it, otherwise not. Later Jinab-i-Amin forwarded some funds, and they were repeatedly written to, asking them to consult with him in all matters and act according to his judgment
selected.reason: Joyful giving paired with consultation and trusted administration.

selected.text: The offerings of that beloved one, which in truth were each like a cutting sword for the day of mourning, like a rain-bearing cloud for the day of thirst, and like a brilliant light for the day of eclipse and night of darkness, arrived and at that very moment were graced with the gaze, and this is a true testimony to the sincerity, sanctity and purity of that beloved's deeds. God suffices as witness. Glory be to God, its radiance almost veiled the light of the sun despite its brilliance and splendor. Since the manifestations of these matters and the appearance of these causes are in truth from the effulgences of the Luminary of the love of God, therefore whatever is mentioned or flows from the tongue has been and is befitting. The Water of Life flows from the spring of love and the comfort of the world exists through its comfort. Blessed is the soul that has attained unto it
selected.reason: Substantive imagery relates the worth of gifts to love.

selected.text: Since your departure nearly a year ago, very little has been received. Though the Cause rests with God, exalted be His glory, this is meant to inform you. Regarding what you wrote about borrowing if necessary from his honor Afnan or Haji Shaykh Muhammad-'Ali, upon them both be the Most Glorious Glory of God, nothing has been borrowed yet.
selected.reason: Acknowledges scarcity and distinguishes proposed borrowing from actual debt.

selected.text: The mention of the souls of the emigrants that you had written was presented at the Holy Court. Blessed be they! In truth, your honor is the cause of blessings to the world, for it was observed that for every soul you have mentioned, divine favor was manifested towards them, even if they were among the most sinful of creation, without any concealment.
selected.reason: Remembrance and favor extend beyond assumptions of personal merit.

selected.text: The details about the trees that were sent will surely be mentioned by him. In truth, he himself is like a tree - God willing, he will appear with sweet fruits. They said: "Blessed is he who sent it and blessed is he, for what he hath done in the path of God, the Lord of the worlds, hath been accepted before the Wronged One." Although the wild rose did not arrive, the deed of the sender and his honor are accepted before God - meaning there is no difference whether it arrived or not.
selected.reason: Intention and effort accepted even when a sent plant fails to arrive.

selected.text: The ring-watch that you had sent to the Most Holy Court was forwarded so that you might sell it and distribute its proceeds among certain handmaidens of God there. One third should be given to Sayfu'llah, that is, the Guest of Baha'u'llah, and the remaining two thirds should be divided between their two sisters and the sisters of Aqa Muhammad-Rida
selected.reason: A jewelry gift sold to support specified people.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about Ghulam -- upon him be the glory of the All-Merciful -- having allocated funds to be delivered over four months by him who serveth the Cause -- upon him be the glory of God and His loving-kindness -- they commanded that two months thereof be [delivered] to the teachers -- upon them be the glory of God, His loving-kindness and His mercy
selected.reason: Contributions provide planned support for teachers.

selected.text: The fragrant flowers sent by the aforementioned one, upon him be God's peace, arrived. They were both used in his presence at the time of breaking the fast and also given to the friends.
selected.reason: Flowers shared with friends rather than retained privately.

selected.text: Additionally, according to the blessed command, if there be any Huququ'llah available with the aforementioned Haji, fifty [...] should be taken and distributed among the loved ones of God and the children of those who were martyred in His path, and the handmaidens who remain without spouse, according to the following details: Baba, upon him be the glory of God [...] the sons of 'Abdu'l-Wahhab Bey who was martyred in the path of God [...] the handmaids of God who remain without spouse, the wife of Mirza Khuda-Virdi who left her husband and believed in God [...] the wife of 'Abdu'l-Fattah who was martyred in His path [...] the sister of Najaf-'Ali 'Amu who believed in God [...] [Mah] Bibi 'Ammih [...] five tumans [...] … Furthermore, broadcloth should be purchased and given to Asadu'llah Bey who was a servant of the Cause
selected.reason: Relief targets widows and martyrs' children; source gaps must remain visible.

selected.text: And as to what his honor Ibn-i-'Attar, upon him be My Glory and loving-kindness, wrote regarding the sum he wished to spend according to ancient custom for the Mother of the Near Ones, upon her be My Glory and loving-kindness: according to the wish of My Name Jamal, upon him be My Glory and mercy, it was given to one of the leaves of the Tree. Excellent is what Ibn-i-'Attar hath done
selected.reason: Customary memorial expenditure redirected to a living recipient.

selected.text: what thou didst write regarding the nisab---whether permission is given to give unto the poor or not---it was submitted. He said: "We grant you
selected.reason: Explicit question about giving an assessed amount to the poor.

selected.text: Some receipts were previously sent. It appears some may have been sent repeatedly. Please review and inform which ones have arrived … The point is that receipts for these three items have been given twice, and that beloved one should be informed of this
selected.reason: Duplicate receipts require reconciliation against the actual gift record.

selected.text: Now, since they have written that the sum is not available with his honor the Big, according to the command his honor Haji Mirza Abu'l-Hasan must settle this debt. … His honor Muhammad Big, upon him be the glory of God, has always been and continues to be mentioned in the Most Holy Court. His services and labors are likewise remembered and witnessed before the Truth
selected.reason: An intermediary settles a debt when the original payer has no funds, revealing practical stewardship.

selected.text: Furthermore, two boxes of tea arrived. He said the tea was very fine, but suited for princes rather than for prisoners and the poor. Its fragrance was excellent, but as it contained white buds, its color was very light. Prison tea should be closer to commercial grade, meaning that a small measure should color multiple cups.
selected.reason: The fitness of a gift is judged against the modest needs of prisoners, not luxury.

selected.text: As for the onion and white poplar cutting that were mentioned and sent, God willing, from the former may colorful flowers appear, and from the latter, refined, wondrous, and sublime shadows, for it exists in the shade. God willing, shade too shall be bestowed upon it, that the friends of God may rest in its shadow and be appropriately gladdened, attaining to the greatest joy, which is the station of nearness to God, exalted be His glory, and may hearken to the divine glorification and sanctification in its rustling.
selected.reason: A planted gift becomes flowers and shade for the rest and fellowship of friends.

selected.text: The paper, rose seeds, narcissus and hyacinth bulbs that were sent have arrived. God willing, the former will be honored with writing and the latter with planting.
selected.reason: Donated paper and plants are put to their intended use.

selected.text: an ablution vessel which has twice been blessed by contact with the sacred Person has been bestowed specially upon your honor. God willing, may you be blessed with this supreme bounty. Likewise, a cloak has been specially bestowed upon his honor Aqa Muhammad Sadiq
selected.reason: A vessel used for worship and a cloak exemplify gifts returned to individual recipients.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about the claims of certain ones - there is no doubt that the creditors are embarrassed while those who should pay show no shame on their faces. This is not new but has always been thus, hence it was said: "A loan is scissors that cut affection."
selected.reason: The warning that loans can cut affection supplies an essential qualification concerning debt.

selected.text: Whatever remaineth of the funds from the land of Kha hath been designated for the poor of this land. Let it arrive and be delivered.
selected.reason: The remainder of a named fund is expressly designated for the poor.

selected.text: Two days ago they brought a rosewater sprinkler with rosewater into His presence. They used it and mentioned Jinab-i-Shaykh.
selected.reason: Use of a gift sustains remembrance of its giver.

selected.text: Some days ago they cut a coat for the blessed body and graciously bestowed one garment of wool to be sent to you. This servant has nothing worthy present except half a container of the finest tea available - that is, the finest that exists in this land - and two or three servings of extremely excellent tea that came from India in previous years.
selected.reason: Reciprocity can take the form of a small gift from limited personal supplies.

selected.text: Know thou that God hath accepted from thee what thou didst dedicate specially to Him from the land which He bestowed upon thee
selected.reason: Dedication of land acknowledges that the giver first received it from God.

selected.text: Something hath been prepared by the Wronged One, though it be but a trifle, and sent to thee that thou mayest know of My love for thee and My care for thee.
selected.reason: A small returned gift communicates love and attentive care.

selected.text: Although outwardly at the time of death the wealthy one did not attain unto faith, yet due to thy connection with him, his cry was answered and a portion of his wealth attained unto acceptance by God.
selected.reason: A particular acceptance from a deceased wealthy man requires careful historical qualification alongside later fund rules.

selected.text: whatever each person sent arrived complete according to what was written, and the details were presented at the Most Holy Court, and all were adorned with the ornament of divine favor and mention of God, exalted be His glory. Of the fruit from that beloved one's garden which was especially honored to reach His presence, He partook of several pieces
selected.reason: Acknowledgment accounts for the different gifts recorded for every contributor.

selected.text: A letter from the handmaidens of God - Hajar, Begum, Khadijih, Maryam, and the wife of Muhammad Ja'far, and another Khadijih, upon them be the Glory of God - in the amount of four tumans was received by the servant in the Prison through the beloved and honored Aqa Mirza Asadu'llah, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, in the sacred month of Dhi'l-Hajjih in the year 1303.
selected.reason: A joint contribution records the participation of six named women.

selected.text: Verily, He answers whosoever calls upon Him, remembers whosoever remembers Him, and draws nigh unto whosoever draws nigh unto Him. He is indeed the All-Bountiful, the Kind.
selected.reason: Mutual remembrance provides a spiritual frame for acknowledgment.

selected.text: Upon thee be My glory. The deeds of the Afnan were observed, and upon him rest My glory, My loving-kindness, and My mercy. He was blessed through the effulgent rays of the luminous Orb of acceptance. Blessed is he, then blessed is he, for he saved others. He is the sign of divine assistance, having aided one of the friends of God
selected.reason: Aid to a friend is recognized as practical divine assistance.

selected.text: Although mint is available, yet if they insist on sending it, there is no harm. In truth, his mint has spread throughout the world.
selected.reason: An available commodity can still be accepted when the giver insists, qualifying necessity.

selected.text: Should any soul be able and willing to render assistance, this would be acceptable and beloved in the sight of God, and would be rewarded
selected.reason: Ability and willingness explicitly condition acceptable assistance.

selected.text: We have sent thee an apple that thou mayest inhale from it the fragrance of the Beloved and the breath of the Adored One.
selected.reason: A simple apple conveys remembrance and spiritual affection.

selected.text: Your letter hath been read before the Throne, and We have accepted what thou didst intend for the sake of God, the Lord of the worlds
selected.reason: Intention for the sake of God grounds acceptance.

selected.text: Instructions have been given to bring funds to that region. After receiving them, safeguard them and send word. Likewise, whatever arrives from anywhere should remain in that land until word is received.
selected.reason: Entrusted funds must be safeguarded and held until further instructions.

selected.text: Regarding the water you have dedicated to the martyrs to be used at the pure resting place of the martyred Shatir Hasan and the martyred Jinab-i-Aqa Asadu'llah, this dedication is most acceptable
selected.reason: Dedicated water serves the memorial resting places of martyrs.

selected.text: Regarding Jinab-i-Binesh, if it is as he himself has written, carry it out and do not request the Huquq, and from time to time inquire about his condition. If he experiences hardship, give him the specified amount
selected.reason: A person in hardship should receive aid instead of being asked for dues.

selected.text: The travel expenses, praise be to God, are ready and prepared. Therefore, the sum that had been sent was most acceptable, but since it was not needed, it was returned … Therefore, quickly return this sum to its owners, the spiritual friends, and offer my utmost apologies so they may spend it themselves for charitable purposes
selected.reason: Unneeded travel money is returned promptly for the donors to use charitably.

selected.text: Indeed you went to great trouble regarding the transfer and burial place of his holiness the Afnan of the Divine Lote Tree. Now you must also bear the burden of debt.
selected.reason: Burial service entails a remaining burden of debt requiring attention.

selected.text: Accept from them this charitable contribution and increase and bless their wealth so they may receive manifold what they have spent in Thy path.
selected.reason: A prayer asks acceptance and blessing for charitable contributors.

selected.text: His honor Mirza Rahim Khan truly made an effort. I beseech God that the friends of God may be enabled to serve the distinguished person. The friends of God must be appreciative - if they see effort and kindness from a distinguished person, they should serve with utmost truthfulness and faithfulness.
selected.reason: Kindness received creates a duty of truthful and faithful appreciation.

selected.text: sum and engage day and night in service. Deliver, therefore, to him every month a hundred dollars, which is equivalent to the sum of twenty pounds. I shall gradually send the sum. The sum of 32/10/0 English pounds, which thou hadst sent through the Anglo-Egyptian Bank, has been received
selected.reason: A specified monthly allowance supports continuing service.

selected.text: You must certainly show them consideration in all respects. Definitely provide them fifteen tomans each month, and if they request somewhat more than this, provide that as well
selected.reason: A regular allowance is supplemented when recipients need more.

selected.text: At first in this partnership, proper consideration was not given to conditions of harmony for the future, thus these difficulties have arisen.
selected.reason: Partnership difficulties expose the need to agree conditions harmoniously at the outset.

selected.text: In the previous year thou didst assist the survivors of the martyrs of Yazd and didst win the polo ball of precedence from the field of endeavor. That charitable giving was accepted and beloved in the sight of the people of effulgence
selected.reason: Assistance to survivors of persecution is explicitly acknowledged.

selected.text: You have caused the names of the bird of the garden of faithfulness who ascended to God and attained to the Most Glorious Kingdom, the possessor of manifest grace, Aqa Siyyid 'Ali, and the mention of the servant of the Twin Shining Lights who attained the presence of his Lord in the seat of truth, Aqa Ghulam-Husayn, to become known and renowned once again, for you made a contribution to the edifice of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar on their behalf.
selected.reason: Contributions in memory of deceased friends renew their remembrance.

selected.text: I became exceedingly pleased with thee because thou didst assist in clearing the debt of the Orient-Occident Unity. Similarly I became infinitely pleased with his honor Mr. Hoar and Mr. and Mrs. Gregory, because they cooperated with you to lift this debt of the Society.
selected.reason: Cooperation clears the debt of an organization devoted to unity.

selected.text: Despite straitened circumstances, I do not wish to be deprived of this great bounty and I am presenting one thousand tumans now, and afterwards at any possible time I will present more.
selected.reason: A personal contribution amid straitened circumstances reveals the meaning of participation.

selected.text: the contributions from the children and women - those skeins are spiritual treasure and those weavings pure gold of perfect standard, acceptable at the threshold of the Blessed Beauty, for they are contributions for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar in the Western lands
selected.reason: The labor of women and children is valued as spiritual treasure in a common undertaking.

selected.text: You must strive night and day to pay the debts and be freed from these entanglements.
selected.reason: Repayment of debt is an urgent practical responsibility.

selected.text: Regarding your selfless sacrifice you had written that whatever you had has been lost - my hope is that it will be compensated. Verily your Lord is the Generous Giver.
selected.reason: Loss incurred in sacrifice is met with hope and consolation.

selected.text: to God that through thy endeavor and magnanimity useful results were produced. I hope the believers of God will become able to pay the 200,000 dollars which they have pledged themselves to contribute
selected.reason: A collective pledge is distinguished from the effort still needed to fulfill it.

selected.text: The carriage that you sent was very acceptable and appropriate. The divine loved ones and this evanescent servant ride in it during the days of pilgrimage and reach the Holy Shrine in perfect comfort
selected.reason: A carriage gift meets the concrete travel needs of pilgrims.

selected.text: Amin has repeatedly offered the utmost praise for your attraction and love, that truly you are firm in faith and steadfast in the Covenant and servants of the Threshold, and whatever was entrusted to them was fully delivered after the flight of the late Khan
selected.reason: Entrusted property is fully delivered following a death.

selected.text: The sum that thou hadst offered through the Spiritual Assembly was accepted
selected.reason: A gift offered through an Assembly illustrates an institutional channel.

selected.text: The garden that the late Aqa Muhammad Baqir and his wife, the handmaiden of God, dedicated to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar has been accepted at the threshold of the Blessed Beauty.
selected.reason: A couple dedicates a garden for communal worship.

selected.text: The contribution they have made for the expenses of the Holy House and crystal wall coverings is accepted at the threshold of oneness. Likewise the contribution you have intended to collect for the poor among the friends - if such contributions are collected, send them for the survivors of the martyrs of Yazd.
selected.reason: Different donations are directed to building and to survivors according to purpose.

selected.text: You had written that you have presented a spice shop as a gift to 'Abdu'l-Baha. This gift is accepted, but you should sell it and spend its proceeds on the poor among the friends.
selected.reason: A gift of a shop is accepted and its proceeds directed to the poor.

selected.text: Until now, you have done more than could be borne. Now again, please make an effort regarding the monthly allowance for these survivors of the martyrs as before, and indicate whatever amount is needed so that it may be offered.
selected.reason: Continuing assistance requires a stated monthly need and recognition of the helper's burden.

selected.text: If you have prepared this from your own funds, spend half of it for the sisters and send the other half to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar. And if it is from others, refer back to the donors and carry out whatever they are satisfied with
selected.reason: Donors must be consulted before funds belonging to others are redirected.

selected.text: In America funds arrived from the Afnan and Abbasov, and likewise the two hundred pounds from Baqiroff arrived. Be assured, and whatever arrived in Paris, receipts were written to Jinab-i-Haji and Jinab-i-Baqiroff. If anything has not had a receipt sent, it has not arrived.
selected.reason: Receipts distinguish funds actually received from those still missing.

selected.text: They even offered two thousand English pounds for travel expenses with extreme pleading and supplication for acceptance, but it was absolutely refused and returned.
selected.reason: Insistent offers for travel expenses can still be refused and returned.

selected.text: from the Rights of God received in the land of Ta [Tehran], the sum of ten tumans monthly has been allocated to you
selected.reason: Funds from the Rights of God are assigned to a monthly allowance.

selected.text: In any case, thou must feel boundless gratitude to His Holiness Mustafa, for that blessed being delivered thee from the pit of error and raised thee to the zenith of the moon of guidance. What bounty is greater than this and what grace mightier than that?
selected.reason: Gratitude for guidance broadens the meaning of a gift beyond material support.

selected.text: Thy gift is much appreciated and very acceptable. I was made very, very happy and I prayed for thee that thou mayest appreciate the contents and significance of it.
selected.reason: Receiving a gift includes reflection on its significance and prayer for the giver.

selected.text: Now is not the time to send that craft to the Holy Threshold. God willing, its time will come and you will be informed. Ask God that its time may arrive, for it will be the cause of bounty.
selected.reason: Acceptance of a craft depends on the appropriate time and circumstances.

selected.text: Accept what they have offered before this servant of Thine and make it a treasure for them in Thy dominion, and make each grain thereof yield seven ears, and in each ear a hundred grains
selected.reason: The image of grain yielding many ears expresses the spiritual fruitfulness of giving.

selected.text: Regarding the piece of land you had written about selling and using the proceeds for the Cause of God - do not hurry now. Let the piece of land remain.
selected.reason: A proposed sale of land is deferred, qualifying zeal with patience.

selected.text: Therefore their worldly affairs and livelihood have fallen into extreme difficulty, and in such cases the friends must certainly assist one another. … Therefore, without mentioning their names or allowing anyone to catch wind of it in a way that would cause them humiliation, rather privately tell the friends that 'Abdu'l-Baha has written that assistance should be collected and sent for one of the dear friends of God
selected.reason: Relief must protect recipients from exposure and humiliation.

selected.text: The honored Hakim-Bashi makes sacrifices in all affairs and strives in the path of God with his wealth and his soul. However, beyond his capacity and means, some time ago he sent an amount of one thousand tumans, and it was written to his honor not to present anything further since the expenses for hosting the friends and those who pass through Qazvin are considerable. Despite this, he has again presented another thousand tumans.
selected.reason: Generosity beyond capacity calls for restraint because other duties already consume resources.

selected.text: Since you requested to personally cover the expenses of the 'Ishqabad school, we have also accepted this.
selected.reason: A willing contributor assumes the expenses of a school.

selected.text: through the efforts of the honorable Consul and respected individuals, a remedy was found. Despite there being absolutely no prior acquaintance between us, they truly made great efforts and showed the utmost chivalry in their care.
selected.reason: Appreciation recognizes aid from strangers without prior acquaintance.

selected.text: Thank the maid-servant of God .... for she hath guided thee to this Path and declared to thee the Call of God. Shouldst thou offer all the treasures of the earth to her, they would not equal this great guidance
selected.reason: The value of guidance exceeds material repayment.

selected.text: As to the expenses of the trip which you have given for the poor, it is very agreeable. This is greater than meeting me.
selected.reason: Giving travel expenses to the poor is valued above a personal meeting.

selected.text: The testimony of Amin is heart-warming, for he hath no thoughts of self, is self-effacing in the Cause, possesseth a pure heart and a radiant soul. Therefore the praise he hath rendered regarding thee is acceptable at the Divine Threshold
selected.reason: A trustee's selflessness gives weight to his testimony.

selected.text: your services will never be forgotten from memory and day by day appear more prominent before our eyes. And likewise the trouble you took during the previous journey and this journey to Paris - all is before our eyes
selected.reason: The practical labor of hospitality and travel support remains remembered.

selected.text: Due to lack of time and opportunity, I have no rest day or night. Still I cannot respond to even one-tenth of the letters. Yet with heart and soul I beseech divine bounties from the All-Merciful for you.
selected.reason: Unanswered letters do not imply lack of remembrance or prayer.

selected.text: The needlework band was accepted, and glory be upon you. … Since Jinab-i-Amin mentioned that you wove the band with your own hands, thus out of kindness it was greatly accepted, and glory be upon you
selected.reason: A gift made by the giver's own hands receives particular appreciation.

selected.text: And arrangements were made for his travel to such a degree that if possible, the Spiritual Assembly should also provide some assistance to him in this regard, and if it is not possible, then so be it
selected.reason: Assembly assistance for travel is expressly conditional on ability.

selected.text: The short treatise which thou hast written upon "Service in the Kingdom," forwarding it here and asking permission for its publication, was read. Spread it among the believers.
selected.reason: A written treatment of service is received and permitted to circulate.

selected.text: Write down the matters in your father's letter and request a receipt from the servant to be written and sent so that it may be sealed.
selected.reason: Written records and sealed receipts support accountability.

selected.text: Therefore, if any of the loved ones of God were to present him with an amount from the Huquq and obtain a receipt, and submit the receipt, this would be accepted, beloved and credited in the sight of God.
selected.reason: An authorized payment channel requires a receipt for credit.

selected.text: As you sent the Huquq with utmost love, therefore this small amount was accepted as a great treasure.
selected.reason: Love makes a small payment a great treasure.

selected.text: Regarding the one hundred pieces of embossed tiles of new design which thou didst write that thou hadst presented to the blessed House - the Afnans should find a place in the House and, as far as possible, make use of them.
selected.reason: A donated craft is to be used where practical in a sacred building.

selected.text: Although I summoned you urgently by telegram from India for an important matter, nevertheless I am writing this letter in response to your communication. … Regarding the purchase of two houses adjacent to the Shrine that you had written about, I wrote to Aqa Siyyid Mahdi that first Aqa Siyyid Isma'il must fully pay off his debts, and then attend to this important task. God willing, there will be no shortcoming in this matter concerning you
selected.reason: Debts must be paid before further property purchases.

selected.text: and his hardships without end; he has, in truth, become helpless. If, each month, five tumans from the funds should arrive, present it to him with the utmost shamefacedness and apology
selected.reason: A recurring allowance is offered with humility toward the distressed recipient.

selected.text: Among the proofs of this is that your honor has shown kindness and rendered service to Jinab-i-Furughi by lending him a sum of money, and this kindness has been accepted in the Most Glorious Kingdom. This loan
selected.reason: A loan can itself be a service, qualifying blanket readings of warnings about debt.

selected.text: of 'Abdu'l-Baha! At this moment, near the Holy Shrine, I have taken in my own hands the vase which you had sent as a memento of my journey to America, and placed it in the Holy Shrine. This is a token of the love, illumination and spirituality of you all
selected.reason: A shared memorial gift expresses the love of a community.

selected.text: Thanks and praise be unto God for that He granted thee a good descendant and dilated thy breast by this great bounty. … It is incumbent on thee to offer many thanks to the Merciful Lord for this great favor in the world of humanity
selected.reason: The birth of a child is received as a gift calling for gratitude.

selected.text: O Gift of God! Thou art mentioned at the Threshold of Oneness and renowned in the gathering of the All-Merciful. Thou didst make a noble effort and didst show forth a shining hand in contributing to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar. Once again thou hast assisted in its repair
selected.reason: Contributing includes repair and maintenance as well as initial construction.

selected.text: The drafts that you sent from 'Ishqabad and Baku both arrived and were sent to Afnan Aqa Mirza Muhsin so that he could write up the receipts and send them to be sealed and forwarded
selected.reason: Receipts are prepared, sealed and forwarded for remittances from different places.

selected.text: They brought two thousand two hundred pieces of gold at a time when means were entirely lacking, and it was spent in that place
selected.reason: Timely aid arrives when means are entirely lacking.

selected.text: Verily, I read thy brilliant letter and thanked God for that He hath created a maid-servant for Baha, who prays for 'Abdu'l-Baha and begs a blessing through the abundance of the favor of God for him ('Abdu'l-Baha) and his household
selected.reason: Prayer for another and his household is itself received with gratitude.

selected.text: The chamber that thou hast made into a Mashriqu'l-Adhkar and a gathering place for the mention of the divine Beauty hath been accepted … thy service shall be accepted and renowned at the threshold of the All-Forgiving Lord
selected.reason: A room offered for common worship illustrates service within ordinary resources.

selected.text: If possible, and if it causes no hardship, assistance should be rendered to Jinab-i-Nayyir and Sina. This would be most acceptable at the Sacred Threshold.
selected.reason: Assistance is welcomed only if possible and without hardship.

selected.text: Service to the Cause of God is among the greatest divine gifts. Praise be to God that you are confirmed in this.
selected.reason: The opportunity to serve is itself a divine gift.

selected.text: Since the loved ones of God in Persia are regarded as veteran friends, it is by virtue of the tremendous affection I cherish for them that their offerings for Huquq are accepted.
selected.reason: Mandatory authorized quotation: exact authorized paragraph presents acceptance of Huquq in the frame of affection.

selected.text: A basket of oranges has been sent. When the friends gather in the evening, present them to the loved ones
selected.reason: A gift of fruit is shared among friends at their gathering.

selected.text: I wrote to Khanum, I am writing to you as well: Should major incidental expenses occur, you may every month obtain up to five Liras from Aqa Mirza Muhsin
selected.reason: An allowance provides for major incidental expenses within a stated limit.

selected.text: The steadfast friends of God are blessed with heavenly sustenance and their poverty draws them near to the divine threshold. They neither complain of poverty nor boast of wealth.
selected.reason: Neither poverty nor wealth should lead to complaint or boasting.

selected.text: The gift sent by the dear handmaiden of God, Liza Khanum - six pieces of handkerchief and two pieces embroidered with the blessed word "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha" - was received through the late Haji Qalandar.
selected.reason: Women's embroidered work gives a concrete example of personal craft.

selected.text: The three shares of the inherited property which thou didst dedicate as an endowment for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar was accepted at the Divine Threshold.
selected.reason: Shares of inherited property are dedicated as an endowment.

selected.text: Multiple prayers and letters were written and sent regarding the schools of Hamadan and those souls who have arisen to provide assistance, as well as those blessed souls who give contributions for teaching.
selected.reason: Assistance to schools and teaching receives prayerful acknowledgment.

selected.text: You truly demonstrated great effort in protecting and preserving those letters. I hope that you will always be successful in safeguarding and preservation.
selected.reason: Preserving letters is recognized as a service.

selected.text: A considerable amount of Huquq had been collected in Hamadan; I wrote that all of it should be spent on the children's school, and I pray and beseech confirmation from the Abha Kingdom.
selected.reason: A reported conversation connects collected dues with children's schooling; its report status must remain visible.

selected.text: Then she begged me to accept a bed. As she insisted I could not refuse. The bed was then sent to my room. Before that time I used to sleep on the floor. The bed is yet in my room, the one on which I sleep now.
selected.reason: A reported narrative distinguishes refusal of a large sum from acceptance of a needed bed.

selected.text: For example, now this person who has sent this gift [referring to an American woman who, after one meeting, became so enchanted that despite her lack of belief, she sent a gift which was a barometer] - she is not a believer but she is well-behaved.
selected.reason: A reported gift from a nonbeliever illustrates personal kindness, requiring distinction from institutional fund rules.

selected.text: And concerning what was written about the honored Afnan - upon them be the most glorious of all glory - having hosted a feast, after it was mentioned in the Most Holy Court the Tongue of Grandeur spoke this most exalted word: Verily it was mentioned before Our face. We have veiled its mention lest every corrupt deceiver become aware of it. There is recorded for him from the Supreme Pen the good of this world and the next
selected.reason: Acknowledgment may withhold publicity to protect a generous host.

selected.text: regarding Aqa Muhammad Sadiq from the people of K, they wrote a letter to this servant about the Huquq, as your honor yourself noted on its back. It was presented to the Most Holy, Most Exalted Presence. According to the command, one portion thereof should be given to the deserving ones in that city, and two portions should be sent to Zaynu'l-Muqarribin, for the people of that land are very deserving. … Although these small amounts do not suffice for that land, they are somewhat useful
selected.reason: An explicit distribution divides funds among deserving recipients in two places.

selected.text: two thousand tumans through the late Haji Shaykh, upon him be the Glory of God - one thousand tumans in silk and one thousand in cash - to the Most Holy Court, after being presented it was not accepted until, considering the distress of the aforementioned one, they accepted it to remain with him for trading purposes
selected.reason: An offering is accepted yet left with the contributor for trade, qualifying simple transfer assumptions.

selected.text: Another matter: A letter was received mentioning that a mule belonging to His Holiness Afnan (upon him be all Glory) was sold by Jinab-i-Amin (upon him be the Glory of God, His light and His favors) to Muhammad Bey (upon him be the Glory of God). A letter from the servant arrived requesting that the payment be sent. What kind of situation is this? This payment had no connection to the Holy Threshold that it should be requested. The property belongs to His Holiness Afnan and the payment should reach him. Now, since Jinab-i-Bey does not have the funds available, as commanded, do not request it and pay it from the Huququ'llah.
selected.reason: Ownership of sale proceeds is distinguished from the sacred fund and inability to pay is accommodated.

selected.text: We heard thy mention and mentioned thee, and I am the All-Knowing Rememberer. We saw thee turning toward Us and We turned toward thee, and I am the One with power over what I will. We found the fragrance of thy love and sent thee the musk of inner meanings in the vessels of words, and I am the Bountiful Giver.
selected.reason: A returned message is presented as a response to love and remembrance.

selected.text: As for the Huququ'llah, it was presented before the Most Holy, Most Exalted Presence. According to His command, you should collect it: half to be sent to the Holy Presence and half to be given to the poor of that land. The names of those who have been blessed to pay the Huququ'llah should be sent to the Most Holy, Most Exalted Presence.
selected.reason: A particular allocation divides dues between the Holy Presence and local poor.

selected.text: Another matter: As some funds were needed, twenty tumans were borrowed from the spiritual friend Aqa Muhammad Ibrahim - upon him be the peace of God - which your honor should convey to him. Although at first he was unwilling to accept it, they specifically stated it must reach him and he accepted. Your honor must pay it. And what the friends brought of gaz and other items was received
selected.reason: Repayment of a loan is required even when the lender initially declines.

selected.text: Whosoever has assisted you in service to the Cause has truly rendered service, and his reward rests with Him. Verily, He has power over all things.
selected.reason: Supporting another person's service counts as service.

selected.text: They mentioned that your honor had sent an amount specifically for Zaynu'l-Muqarrabin, upon him be the Glory of God. As commanded, it was left with Aqa Muhammad Javad, upon him be the Glory of God, so that whenever someone travels to Mosul it may be sent. Likewise, on behalf of Mulla Muhammad-'Ali an amount along with a box of tea was left with this lowly one specifically for the aforementioned one. Until now its dispatch has been delayed as no one was traveling. God willing it will be sent. … Whatever has reached Jinab-i-Amin has reached completely and fully, nay even more
selected.reason: Entrusted funds remain designated for their recipient while transport is delayed.

selected.text: Praise be to God that thou hast been enabled to discharge thy debts. "And whosoever placeth his reliance on God, He is sufficient unto him." That which hath been the key to prosperity and the opener of the gate of success was revealed aforetime from the Supreme Pen.
selected.reason: Freedom from debt is received with gratitude and trust.

selected.text: The vases that were sent last were very well received. They said although the Most Great Prison was not and is not a place for using such items, yet since their craftsmanship was refined and perfect, We accepted them, and these bear no resemblance whatsoever to the previous vases.
selected.reason: Refined workmanship can make a gift acceptable despite the restrictions of imprisonment.

selected.text: As for the matter of the shawls that they had written about, that honored one did not write details about how they should be sent. Keeping them here is not advisable as they might be lost. That beloved one should write where and how they should be sent. These days his honor Ha, upon him be Baha'u'llah, has sought to buy them, but his honor Amin is not agreeable. The matter is now pending. If they are given to them, that beloved one will be informed, but in any case that honored one should write details about how they should be sent, as they might not pass with his honor Ha.
selected.reason: Safe custody requires clear instructions about the destination and method of dispatch.

selected.text: according to that list which your honor had sent, wondrous and sublime Tablets were revealed, but there was no one available to carry them. For nearly two years this matter remained in abeyance. Now Jinab-i-Mulla Muhammad-'Ali has insisted that he will carry them, therefore they were sent so that they may be delivered to the mentioned souls
selected.reason: The absence of a carrier explains a long delay in acknowledgments.

selected.text: We praise God that He hath shown thee servants in this Revelation who have hastened to do good works before their appointed time. These, verily, are among the people of Baha. Upon them rest My mercy, My glory, My remembrance, and My praise at all times. These are they whom the world hath not prevented from treading the path of God, the Lord of all names, and who have spent that which they possessed in their quest for that which is with God. We have accepted from them as a bounty from Our presence.
selected.reason: Initiative in doing good qualified by wisdom, timing and freedom in a particular government stipend matter.

selected.text: the vine-cuttings and trees sent by them, both before and after, did arrive; yet, by reason of the abundance of the rains and the vehemence of the winds, they were consigned underground in trust, until within these past two or three days they have been brought forth, and the planting and sowing thereof commenced. In the name of the true Planter and the true Husbandman, and on their behalf, they have been and are being planted. This year the severity of the rains hath disordered the arrangement and work of planting the trees. Such is the decree of our Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. For example, the olive trees were cut off from their place for two months, and it was not possible to set them in the ground, for the soil was but mud
selected.reason: Care for donated plants must respond to weather and practical limitations.

selected.text: The gift that was sent in their name has arrived. Praise be to God Who hath manifested from His presence that which indicateth His love and affection. Think not that there was any hesitation in accepting what was sent. Nay, by the very Self of the Lord, this servant beareth witness that it was accepted with supreme acceptance. The gaze of them that are endued with certitude is fixed upon love and purpose and the sender, not upon aught else.
selected.reason: Acceptance looks to love, purpose and the sender rather than the object alone.

selected.text: As for what thou didst report regarding the house outside the sanctuary, We have held back since this Wronged One had no funds to transfer, and We did not wish to afflict thee with new troubles. The tribulation of the house that has occurred is sufficient for thee.
selected.reason: A proposed property matter is deferred to avoid adding to another's troubles.

selected.text: This was presented in the Most Holy Court and according to command I should send receipts for those funds … He commanded that receipts be sent to each of those souls so that all may rejoice and give thanks to God
selected.reason: Each contributor should receive an individual receipt.

selected.text: Moreover, whatsoever you had sent previously and subsequently, of tea and preserves, arrived completely and perfectly. But what shall I say about the preserves which truly became heavenly food - groups of people were sustained by it, whether from among the assured believers, the sincere faithful ones, the wavering ones, or the heedless ones of the city who have attained to the love of God according to their measure though they have no knowledge of the Cause.
selected.reason: Food gifts sustain people across differences of belief and commitment.

selected.text: Those who have turned to the court of Thy glory and drunk the choice wine of revelation from the hand of Thy bounty and soared in the atmosphere of Thy love, desired to pay Thy rights which Thou didst send down in Thy Book. O Lord! They have spent in Thy love what Thou didst provide them from the treasuries of Thy bounty and favor.
selected.reason: A prayer recognizes that contributions return what divine bounty first supplied.

selected.text: And whatever was commanded should be given to the loved ones - take from the aforementioned amount and give it. The blessed month of Ramadan hath come, assistance to some is necessary.
selected.reason: A season of need calls for timely assistance from entrusted funds.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about obtaining four hundred from two sources - nothing can be obtained from the two mentioned sources. According to what was stated, they have no cash on hand.
selected.reason: Requests for funds must recognize when the proposed sources have no cash.

selected.text: He said that whatever you have spent or may spend on yourself and your family is all beloved and adorned with the ornament of acceptance
selected.reason: Spending for oneself and one's family is expressly accepted.

selected.text: is that at present there are no funds from God's treasury with the aforementioned gentleman, though this servant has one hundred tumans with him. It is hoped that affairs there will proceed with truthfulness, sincerity and uprightness, and that debts will be paid
selected.reason: Institutional and personal balances are distinguished while debts require upright settlement.

selected.text: deliver from the land of Kha the sum of fifty tumans to the honoured Dhabih of the land of K, and the sooner it arrives, the more pleasing it will be in the sight of the Best-Beloved. Likewise, send the sum of one hundred and thirty-three tumans and eight thousand to His Holiness Ismu'llah Jamal - upon him be all the Most Glorious Glory and all the Most Resplendent Light - to be delivered to the heirs of the late Ustad Ahmad who ascended to the Most Exalted Horizon while in prison. Obtain a receipt and forward it to the Most Holy Court
selected.reason: Urgent support for a prisoner's heirs combines compassion with a receipt requirement.

selected.text: And this hath been inscribed in a Tablet wherein the deeds of the doers shall not be omitted by so much as a date-stone's weight or a whit. Soon shall appear in the earth the recompense of what ye have done, and verily He rewardeth His sincere servants.
selected.reason: No sincere deed is lost from remembrance, however small.

selected.text: These sweets have no equal, for they were sent with utmost love and affection and in delicacy have reached the highest summit. They were sent for the sake of God and we gave them away for the sake of God. Well done to the sender, and blessed and wholesome be it to the distributor and giver!
selected.reason: Both sending and redistributing a gift can be done for the sake of God.

selected.text: In these days the widow of the late and elevated Mulla Qasim, upon him be the Glory of God, has sent a letter mentioning that your honor intends to pay the debt of Karbila'i [Hasan]. Blessed are you and joy be unto you, for this deed is considered praiseworthy in all the divine Books, both past and future.
selected.reason: Paying another's debt is recognized through a widow's account.

selected.text: In all matters We have been and are mindful of what benefits the servants themselves, and God is sufficient as witness. … Regarding transactions, if you observe any benefit from your going - that is, if rights can be paid according to divine law without any harm occurring - in this case there is and was no objection
selected.reason: Transactions are acceptable when rights can be met without harm to those involved.

selected.text: O Badi', son of Muhammad-Quli who emigrated and attained unto the name of the Goal of the world! O Badi'! The adults have not attained unto the traces of the Most Exalted Pen, yet thou hast attained.
selected.reason: A child can receive acknowledgment beyond what adults have attained.

selected.text: His honor Afnan desired to take from the treasury of divine knowledge a pearl of utterance as a gift for you and bring it forth. From this desire the light of love shone forth.
selected.reason: Requesting a gift of words for another manifests love.

selected.text: Regarding what was written about the funds - if it refers to the funds of the esteemed Hakim Musa, they were assigned to the beloved and honored Haji Siyyid Javad, upon him be God's peace, and should be in liras. If it refers to other funds, whether mejidiyyes or otherwise makes no difference - they all go back to Aqa Faraj and others like him, upon them be God's peace.
selected.reason: The identity and purpose of funds determine their payment instructions.

selected.text: The message from the spiritual friend His Honor Ghulam-'Ali, upon him be the Glory of God, consisting of one piece of needlework termeh of his own making, was received through His Honor the esteemed Afnan Haji Siyyid 'Ali, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, in the year 1307.
selected.reason: A man's handmade needlework complements the record of women's craft contributions.

selected.text: Regarding the agreed-upon sum about which was written before - the intention was that your honor should record whatever has reached you, meaning the original capital
selected.reason: Stewardship requires recording the original capital actually received.

selected.text: The petition of Jinab-i-Haydar-Qabli-'Ali, upon him be Baha, hath been heard. As to the matter of the fifty tumans belonging to the brothers Naddaf, upon them be the Glory of God, the decree concerning this was already revealed. The portion for the Land of Mim must be sent with haste, that together with the sum forwarded to the Land of Ta, it may reach either the widow of the Most Exalted Martyr, upon him be all the Most Glorious Beauty, or his brother.
selected.reason: Prompt remittance supports the family of a martyr.

selected.text: Your letter attained the presence and as it indicated the great divine bounty and the most great heavenly sustenance, which is the health of being, it brought joy and gladness
selected.reason: Health itself is received as a bounty and a source of shared gladness.

selected.text: That which you sent hath been presented before the Throne. This is of My favor unto you. Then We accepted it, and this is another favor, and We shall clothe it with Our bounties.
selected.reason: Both presentation and acceptance are understood as divine favor.

selected.text: Behold God's faithfulness in the visible realm, in that He hath not forgotten thee, and at the times when seekers turn toward Him, mention of thee hath flowed from the Supreme Pen and thy name hath been recorded in holy Tablets.
selected.reason: Faithfulness is expressed in continuing remembrance.

selected.text: When I reminded them, they said: "Let these six hundred ashrafis be held in trust with you, and give fifty tumans from it as a draft to Haji Amin."
selected.reason: A sum held in trust is distinguished from the portion authorized for transfer.

selected.text: Whatever has befallen you in the path of God's Cause, and likewise the deeds that have been manifested by you for the sake of God - all have flowed from the Most Exalted Pen and been recorded.
selected.reason: Suffering and deeds in service are both remembered.

selected.text: We make mention of him whose name was presented before the Face in this Great Prison. There is no servant but We have mentioned him with grace, and no handmaiden but has attained to My beauteous remembrance.
selected.reason: The scope of remembrance includes every servant and handmaiden.

selected.text: Your letter was received and its contents noted. For a time, due to lack of means, the sending of a reply was delayed.
selected.reason: Lack of means can delay correspondence without diminishing regard.

selected.text: though whatever his eminence Amin, upon him be Baha'u'llah's glory, considers advisable has been and is beloved, since he has no thoughts of self and whatever efforts he has made until now have been for the sake of God
selected.reason: A trustee's advice is valued because his efforts are free from self-interest.

selected.text: That which thou didst send from the heaven of thy love hath come before this servant, and I have forwarded it to the place which thou didst desire.
selected.reason: A gift is forwarded to the destination the donor desired.

selected.text: We have accepted what ye desired in the path of God and have written for you, from My Most Exalted Pen, the reward of what ye intended. By My life! This is a bounty, and this is a mercy, and this is the manifestation of loving-kindness from God
selected.reason: An intended act receives recognition alongside completed giving.

selected.text: Previously, one mithqal of gold was set as an offering for this da'ira, but His Holiness the Exalted - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - granted a reduction. The purpose of the offering is for the person who receives the da'ira. The Manifestations of Truth have never had, nor will ever have, any attachment to this world and what it contains. Whoever received it would spend it, on behalf of the Truth, either for those they knew to be deserving or for other beneficial purposes they deemed appropriate
selected.reason: A historical offering supports its recipient and beneficial purposes rather than attachment to possessions.

selected.text: However, they must pay the Huququ'llah, and this servant mentions this out of sincerity, for this practice has been and is the cause of the purification of wealth and the descent of blessing. Since it was asked what they should do, this servant mentioned the Command of God
selected.reason: Payment of dues is connected with purification and blessing in response to a request for guidance.

selected.text: Similarly, all other items were received. This is quite clear and evident: that any matter which is blended with love is reckoned among the great bounties in the sight of God.
selected.reason: Love transforms even ordinary matters into great bounties.

selected.text: We must be like the fountain or spring that is continually emptying itself of all that it has and is continually being refilled from an invisible source. To be continually giving out for the good of our fellows undeterred by fear of poverty and reliant on the unfailing bounty of the Source of all wealth and all good -- this is the secret of right living.
selected.original: We must be like the fountain or spring that is continually emptying itself of all that it has and is continually being refilled from an invisible source. To be continually giving out for the good of our fellows undeterred by fear of poverty and reliant on the unfailing bounty of the Source of all wealth and all good -- this is the secret of right living. COC#1212, PBA.020, PBA.095
selected.reason: The fountain image gives a central account of continuing generosity and trust.

selected.text: And as the progress and execution of spiritual activities is dependent and conditioned upon material means, it is of absolute necessity that immediately after the establishment of local as well as national Spiritual Assemblies, a Baha'i Fund be established, to be placed under the exclusive control of the Spiritual Assembly. All donations and contributions should be offered to the Treasurer of the Assembly, for the express purpose of promoting the interests of the Cause, throughout that locality or country. selected.text: As the activities of the American Baha'i community expand, and its world-wide prestige correspondingly increases, the institution of the National Fund, the bedrock on which all other institutions must necessarily rest and be established, acquires added importance, and should be increasingly supported by the entire body of the believers, both in their individual capacities, and through their collective efforts, whether organized as groups or as local Assemblies. I am eagerly and prayerfully awaiting the news of an unprecedented expansion in so vital an organ of the administrative Order of the Faith.

selected.text: He wishes me to stress again that under no circumstances the believers should accept any financial help from non-Baha'is for use in connection with specific administrative activities of the Faith such as the Temple construction fund, and other local or national Baha'i administrative funds. The reasons for this is twofold: First because the institutions which the Baha'is are gradually building are in the nature of gifts from Baha'u'llah to the world; and secondly the acceptance of funds from non-believers for specific Baha'i use would, sooner or later, involve the Baha'is into unforseen and difficulties with other, and thus cause incalculable harm to the body of the Cause.

selected.reference: LG#413 (8 Dec. 1947 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: In the first place every believer is free to follow the dictates of his own conscience as regards the manner in which to spend his own money. Secondly, we must always bear in mind that there are so few Baha'is in the world, relative to the world's population, and so many people in need, that even if all of us gave all we had, it would not alleviate more than an infinitesimal amount of suffering. This does not mean we must not help the needy, we should; but our contributions to the Faith are the surest way of lifting once and for all time the burden of hunger and misery from mankind, for it is only through the System of Baha'u'llah--Divine in origin--that the world can be gotten on its feet, and want, fear, hunger, war, etc., be eliminated. Non-Baha'is cannot contribute to our work or do it for us; so really our first obligation is to support our own teaching work, as this will lead to the healing of the nations.
